summary: Staffed Malheur NF L-4 on a 32-foot tower, built 1949 to replace a 1932 15-foot L-4 cab; listed on the NHLR; access road gated below the lookout.

access.note: Staffed Forest Service lookout. The directory lists the site as legally accessible; a 2018 visit noted a gate on the access road about 0.6 miles below the lookout.

visit.trail_note: A gate on the access road about 0.6 miles below the lookout (2018 visit).

events.note: First lookout, a 15-foot L-4 cab. The Oregon Lookouts history dates the first tower to 1933.
A 16 x 18 garage built at the site.
Malheur Historical Record 1943-1953 note: new house and tower; old house replaced though actually fairly good.
Present L-4 cab on a 32-foot treated timber tower replaced the first lookout.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register July 16, 2002.
Visit on May 25, 2018 lists the lookout as Staffed.
Listed as Staffed in the July 2026 directory.

corrections.why: 4.6 m is 15 feet, the height of the first 1932 L-4 cab. The present cab stands on a 32-foot treated timber tower, about 9.8 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout give 1932 for the first 15-foot L-4. The Oregon Lookouts history gives 1933. The story reports both.
The register gives 6,002 ft (1,829 m), which matches the brief. Firelookout and the 2026 directory give 6,128 ft. The record keeps the register figure; the story gives no elevation.

Register, firelookout and Oregon Lookouts date the present L-4 tower to 1949. A 1948 note in the Malheur Historical Record already describes a new house and tower. The story reports the 1949 date and the 1948 note.

The register says the site is in active service and firelookout says it is available for emergencies. The 2018 visit and 2026 directory say staffed. The story reports the staffed listing and both sources' wording.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 4.6 is the first 15-foot cab; corrected to the present 32-foot tower (9.8 m). Brief elevation matches the register. Current use is only known from the 2018 visit and the 2026 directory. No recent access or rental source was found; a web search for a Harney County Sugarloaf lookout turned up nothing usable. The brief's cid -2 record may duplicate another Sugarloaf entry in the Malheur records; not checked.
